1	# CommerceForge Dev Docs — Build for the Commerce Platform
     2	
     3	## Brand
     4	CommerceForge is a developer documentation hub for building apps, storefronts, and AI-powered shopping agents on a leading ecommerce platform. The docs guide developers through building, customizing, and launching commerce experiences with clear documentation, CLI tooling, and community resources.
     5	
     6	Brand colors: #000000 (primary/background), #475F91 (accent/link blue), #FFFFFF (text/foreground)
     7	
     8	Tone: Professional, modern, minimal. Dark mode default.
     9	
    10	## Hero Content
    11	Title: CommerceForge Dev Docs
    12	Subtitle: Learn how to build an app, or customize your storefront. Whether you're just getting started, deep in the development process, or ready to distribute and monetize your work, CommerceForge's docs, dev tools and frameworks make building easy and efficient.
    13	CTA: "Build your first app →" | "Build a storefront →" | "Build agents with UCP →"
    14	
    15	## Product Areas
    16	- **Apps** — Extend CommerceForge's core functionality with apps that integrate into the admin, online store, checkout and more. CTA: "Build your first app →"
    17	- **Storefronts** — Help merchants express their unique brand by building a custom theme or Hydrogen storefront. CTA: "Build a storefront →"
    18	- **Agents** — Build agentic shopping experiences powered by CommerceForge merchants, from product discovery to checkout. CTA: "Build agents with UCP →"
    19	
    20	## CLI Quick-Start
    21	Title: Accelerate development with CommerceForge CLI 3.0
    22	Subtitle: Initialize new apps, themes, and headless storefronts in an instant with the latest CommerceForge CLI. A single command installs all the dependencies you need, including the CLI itself, so you can dive straight into development.
    23	
    24	**Apps accordion:**
    25	1. Install CommerceForge CLI globally.
    26	2. Navigate to the directory where you want to create your app.
    27	3. Run the second command to create a new app. Your app will be added as a new subdirectory.
    28	
    29	**Themes accordion:**
    30	1. Install CommerceForge CLI globally.
    31	2. Navigate to the directory where you want to create your theme.
    32	3. Run the second command to clone a starter theme. Your theme will be created in a new subdirectory.
    33	
    34	**Headless storefronts accordion:**
    35	1. Install CommerceForge CLI globally.
    36	2. Navigate to the directory where you want to create your Hydrogen storefront.
    37	3. Run the second command to initialize a Hydrogen storefront in a new subdirectory.
    38	
    39	Install commands (tabbed):
    40	- **npm:** `npm i -g @commerceforge/cli@latest`
    41	- **yarn:** `yarn global add @commerceforge/cli@latest`
    42	- **pnpm:** `pnpm add -g @commerceforge/cli@latest`
    43	
    44	Init commands:
    45	- Apps: `commerceforge app init`
    46	- Themes: `commerceforge theme init`
    47	- Storefronts: `commerceforge hydrogen init`
    48	
    49	## Launch CTA
    50	**App Marketplace** — When you're ready, submit your app to the CommerceForge App Marketplace so merchants can find and buy your app through search or personalized recommendations. CTA: "See App Marketplace requirements →"
    51	
    52	**Theme Store** — Promote and sell your custom theme to merchants building their brands on the CommerceForge Theme Store. CTA: "See Theme Store requirements →"
    53	
    54	## Community Resources
    55	- **Dev Community →** — Q&A and advice from CommerceForge community experts
    56	- **Developer Changelog →** — The latest CommerceForge ecosystem updates
    57	- **YouTube channel →** — Tips and insights in dev and design
    58	- **Partners blog →** — Educational resources and product previews
    59	
    60	## App Surfaces
    61	Build across every surface from a single app. All UI surfaces share Polaris, CommerceForge's unified design system.
    62	- **App Home** — Build your app's main interface in the admin with Polaris web components and App Bridge.
    63	- **Admin** — Add actions, blocks, and print functionality to resource pages in the admin.
    64	- **Checkout** — Customize the checkout experience with UI extensions and backend logic.
    65	- **Customer accounts** — Extend order status pages and the logged-in customer experience.
    66	- **Flow** — Integrate triggers, actions, and templates into the automation platform.
    67	- **Online store** — Add dynamic functionality to merchants' storefront themes.
    68	
    69	## Building Blocks
    70	Read and write store data with APIs, react to events with webhooks, and customize backend behavior with Functions.
    71	- **GraphQL** — Query and mutate products, customers, orders, inventory, and more.
    72	- **Extensions** — Add your app's functionality to user interfaces with app extensions.
    73	- **Functions** — Customize backend logic for discounts, payments, delivery, and cart validation.
    74	- **Webhooks** — Subscribe to store events and trigger your own logic in real time.
    75	- **Metafields** — Extend resources with custom fields and validation rules.
    76	- **Authentication** — Authenticate with CommerceForge and manage access scopes for your app.
    77	
    78	## Use Cases
    79	Integrate with dedicated APIs for specific commerce workflows.
    80	- **Marketing and analytics** — Track customer behavior with web pixels and manage marketing activities.
    81	- **Discounts** — Create custom discount types with Functions and the GraphQL Admin API.
    82	- **Product merchandising** — Manage products, collections, variants, and pricing.
    83	- **Orders and fulfillment** — Manage orders, fulfillments, returns, and shipping workflows.
    84	- **Payments** — Build payment gateways, alternative payments, and redeemable extensions.
    85	- **B2B** — Build for wholesale with company management, catalogs, and draft orders.
    86	
    87	## Best Practices
    88	- **Performance** — Optimize speed across admin, checkout, storefront, and POS.
    89	- **Accessibility** — Make your app usable by everyone, including people with disabilities.
    90	- **Security** — Protect your app and merchant data from common vulnerabilities.
    91	- **Compliance** — Follow API terms and privacy law requirements.
    92	- **Localization** — Translate and adapt your app for international merchants.
    93	- **Non-deceptive code** — Meet requirements for transparent and honest app behavior.
    94	
    95	## Themes & Theming System
    96	**Themes** — Complete customization on CommerceForge's fully managed platform. Tailor the look and feel of your storefront without worrying about servers, security, or scaling.
    97	- **Create a new theme** — Create and preview a starter theme in minutes, using real store data.
    98	- **Customize an existing theme** — Connect an existing theme codebase to start making updates.
    99	
   100	**Theming system highlights:**
   101	- **Powered by Liquid** — A simple and expressive templating language. Mix with standard HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for fully bespoke storefronts.
   102	- **No-code editor, with low-code configuration** — Define composable blocks and sections with a simple JSON schema and let merchants make edits without touching code.
   103	- **Build for the Theme Store** — Create premium themes that work off the shelf, then sell to millions of merchants.
   104	- **Theme app extensions** — Build custom apps to augment storefront functionality.
   105	
   106	## Headless APIs
   107	Full-stack control with advanced commerce APIs. Go headless with composable APIs or use Hydrogen, the official headless framework.
   108	- **Storefront API** — Surface product data anywhere, served from the edge with no rate limits.
   109	- **Customer Account API** — Build personalized commerce into any part of your stack.
   110	- **Storefront Web Components** — Sell products anywhere with a few lines of embedded HTML.
   111	
   112	## Headless Dev Tools
   113	- **Hydrogen** — Skip the boilerplate and start building fast with CommerceForge's batteries-included headless framework, built on top of Remix.
   114	- **Oxygen** — Host Hydrogen apps on Oxygen, a global serverless edge, and preview every update before deploying to production. No extra charge.
   115	
   116	## Mobile Commerce
   117	- **Mobile SDKs** — Build native shopping experiences with SDKs for Android and iOS.
   118	- **Checkout Kit** — Add the world's best performing checkout to your mobile apps.
   119	
   120	## Platform Extensions
   121	- **Customer Account extensions** — Add custom functionality to the customer account experience.
   122	- **Checkout UI extensions** — Customize the world's best-performing checkout.
   123	
   124	## Agentic Commerce Hero
   125	Title: Agentic commerce has arrived
   126	Subtitle: Build unified agentic experiences that securely act on behalf of users by leveraging Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) with CommerceForge MCP servers.
   127	CTA: "Start building" — Authenticate, search the Catalog, and refer buyers to checkout for attribution.
   128	
   129	## Protocol Overview
   130	The Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) is an open standard that establishes a common language and a set of primitives that allow agents, merchants, Payment Service Providers (PSPs), and Credential Providers (CPs) to communicate consistently and securely across the web. CommerceForge provides MCP tools that are UCP-compliant to build with this interoperable and extensible protocol.
   131	
   132	## Protocol Actors
   133	UCP defines interactions between four primary actors:
   134	- **Agent** — Platforms, agents, and applications acting on behalf of buyers
   135	- **Merchant** — Sellers providing products and fulfillment
   136	- **CP** — Credential Providers managing buyer identity and authentication
   137	- **PSP** — Payment Service Providers handling payment processing
   138	
   139	## How It Works
   140	CommerceForge provides MCP tools that implement UCP's core capabilities:
   141	- **Discovery** — Search products across the platform, retrieve details, and help buyers find what they're looking for.
   142	- **Checkout** — Create checkout sessions, collect buyer information, attach payment information, and direct buyers to finish purchases on merchant storefronts.
   143	
   144	## Product Discovery
   145	Agents can query all merchants across the CommerceForge platform, apply relevant filters, and display results buyers can interact with using the Catalog MCP server. Once buyers select a product, agentic apps can retrieve variant details needed to create checkout sessions.
   146	
   147	## Checkout Flow
   148	As buyers select items from the Catalog, agentic apps can create and update carts and checkouts. Apps can refer buyers directly to merchant storefronts to complete checkout. All developers with Catalog access can direct buyers through Checkout, building referral applications and advertising models by controlling marketing attribution on top of UCP.
   149	Status: Coming soon
   150	
   151	## Support Hero
   152	Title: Get answers from Dev Community
   153	Subtitle: Connect with developers and CommerceForge experts to share insights, ask questions, and collaborate on projects.
   154	CTA: "Visit community"
   155	
   156	## Additional Support
   157	For non-technical support, read partner program documentation, or reach out to the support team on the CommerceForge Help Center.
   158	
   159	## Support Categories
   160	- **Partner Program** — CommerceForge Partner Program, Partner Branding
   161	- **Apps** — App Store Review Process, App Distribution
   162	- **Themes** — Theme Store Review Process, Theme Store Requirements
   163	- **Payout** — Payout Management, Leads & Referrals
   164	
   165	## General Queries
   166	For any other non-technical requests, contact the support team.
   167	CTA: "Contact us"
   168	
   169	## Navigation
   170	Top nav: Apps · Storefronts · Agents · References · Help · Log in
   171	Utility: Ask assistant (search) · Dark mode toggle
   172	
   173	## Footer Navigation
   174	**Updates:** Developer changelog · CommerceForge Editions
   175	**Business growth:** CommerceForge Partners Program · CommerceForge App Marketplace · CommerceForge Academy
   176	**Legal:** Terms of service · API terms of use · Privacy policy · Partners Program Agreement
   177	**CommerceForge:** About CommerceForge · CommerceForge Plus · Careers · Investors · Press and media

1	---
     2	name: web-designer
     3	description: >-
     4	  Designs user interfaces with clear information hierarchy, intuitive
     5	  interaction patterns, and accessibility-first layouts. Use when creating
     6	  wireframes, evaluating UX flows, auditing visual hierarchy, designing
     7	  responsive layouts, or improving usability of existing Loom interfaces.
     8	metadata:
     9	  role: Web Designer
    10	  level: ic
    11	  reports_to: product-manager
    12	  specialties:
    13	  - UI/UX design
    14	  - interaction patterns
    15	  - visual hierarchy
    16	  - accessibility
    17	  - responsive layout
    18	  display_name: Charlie Reeves
    19	  author: loom
    20	  version: '3.0'
    21	license: Proprietary
    22	compatibility: Designed for Loom
    23	---
    24	
    25	# Web Designer
    26	
    27	You design how users interact with Loom. Every screen, button, and piece of
    28	information is evaluated from the user's perspective: is it findable, is it
    29	clear, does it respect the user's time?
    30	
    31	## Primary Skill
    32	
    33	Your default lens is user experience. You evaluate interfaces by asking three
    34	questions in order:
    35	
    36	1. **Can the user find it?** (information architecture, navigation, visual hierarchy)
    37	2. **Can the user understand it?** (labels, layout, progressive disclosure)
    38	3. **Can the user complete the task?** (interaction flow, error recovery, feedback)
    39	
    40	### Design workflow
    41	
    42	1. **Clarify the goal** — what user task does this interface serve? Write it as a single sentence.
    43	2. **Map the flow** — sketch the steps from entry to completion. Identify decision points and error states.
    44	3. **Design the layout** — establish visual hierarchy. Primary action prominent, secondary actions accessible but not competing.
    45	4. **Validate accessibility** — check color contrast (WCAG AA minimum), touch targets (44px minimum), keyboard flow, screen reader order.
    46	5. **Review** — walk through the flow as three user types: first-time, returning, power user.
    47	
    48	### Example: designing a bead status filter
    49	
    50	```
    51	Goal: Let users filter the bead list by status (open, in-progress, closed).
    52	
    53	Flow:
    54	  1. User sees bead list (default: all statuses).
    55	  2. User clicks filter control -> dropdown appears with status options.
    56	  3. User selects one or more statuses -> list updates immediately.
    57	  4. Active filters shown as removable chips above the list.
    58	
    59	Layout decisions:
    60	  - Filter control placed top-left, aligned with list header (scan line).
    61	  - Chips use distinct background color with "x" dismiss button (44px target).
    62	  - Empty state: "No beads match this filter" with clear-all action.
    63	
    64	Accessibility:
    65	  - Filter dropdown: aria-haspopup="listbox", arrow key navigation.
    66	  - Chips: role="status" with aria-label "Remove filter: open".
    67	  - Live region announces "Showing 12 beads" on filter change.
    68	```
    69	
    70	## Org Position
    71	
    72	- **Reports to:** Product Manager
    73	- **Direct reports:** None
    74	
    75	## Available Skills
    76	
    77	You are not limited to design. Use other skills when the situation demands it:
    78	
    79	- **Front-end code** — implement your designs directly in HTML, CSS, and JavaScript when that is faster than handing off.
    80	- **Documentation** — update UI screenshots and usage guides when designs change.
    81	- **Backend adjustments** — when a design change requires a small backend tweak (e.g., adding a display field to an API response), make it yourself.
    82	
    83	**When to do it yourself vs delegate:**
    84	- **Do it yourself:** The implementation is straightforward CSS/HTML and you can ship it faster than writing a handoff spec.
    85	- **Delegate:** The change requires complex state management, database changes, or performance-critical code.
    86	- **Call a meeting:** The design affects multiple product areas or changes established interaction patterns.
    87	
    88	## Model Selection
    89	
    90	- **Design decisions** (UX flow, information architecture, interaction patterns): strongest model — nuanced reasoning required
    91	- **CSS/layout implementation** (translating approved designs to code): mid-tier model
    92	- **Quick mockups** (rough wireframes, placeholder layouts): lightweight model

Agents

Agentic commerce has arrived

Build unified agentic experiences that securely act on behalf of users by leveraging Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) with CommerceForge MCP servers.

Start building → How it works →
Protocol

Universal Commerce Protocol

The Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) is an open standard that establishes a common language and a set of primitives that allow agents, merchants, Payment Service Providers (PSPs), and Credential Providers (CPs) to communicate consistently and securely across the web.

Protocol Actors

Agent

Platforms, agents, and applications acting on behalf of buyers

Merchant

Sellers providing products and fulfillment

CP

Credential Providers managing buyer identity and authentication

PSP

Payment Service Providers handling payment processing

CommerceForge provides MCP tools that are UCP-compliant to build with this interoperable and extensible protocol.

Integration

How It Works

CommerceForge provides MCP tools that implement UCP's core capabilities.

Discovery

Search products across the platform, retrieve details, and help buyers find what they're looking for.

Checkout

Create checkout sessions, collect buyer information, attach payment information, and direct buyers to finish purchases on merchant storefronts.

Catalog

Product Discovery

Agents can query all merchants across the CommerceForge platform, apply relevant filters, and display results buyers can interact with using the Catalog MCP server.

Once buyers select a product, agentic apps can retrieve variant details needed to create checkout sessions.

# Search products across all merchants
commerceforge catalog search --query "running shoes" --filter category:footwear
Checkout

Checkout Flow

As buyers select items from the Catalog, agentic apps can create and update carts and checkouts.

Apps can refer buyers directly to merchant storefronts to complete checkout. All developers with Catalog access can direct buyers through Checkout, building referral applications and advertising models by controlling marketing attribution on top of UCP.

# Create a checkout session for selected items
commerceforge checkout create --items item_123,item_456 --referral my-agent-app

steps.message:
The CommerceForge Dev Docs hub is complete. Here's a summary of what was built:

## Output Files (`/app/output/`)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `index.html` | Home page with hero, product cards, CLI accordion + tabs, launch CTAs, community links |
| `apps-build.html` | Apps docs page with collapsible sidebar, dev tools, surfaces grid, building blocks, use cases, best practices |
| `storefronts.html` | Storefronts page with sidebar, themes, theming system, headless APIs, dev tools, mobile commerce, platform extensions |
| `agents.html` | Agents page with sidebar, UCP protocol overview, actor diagram, how it works, product discovery, checkout flow |
| `support.html` | Support page with hero, support category cards, general queries contact CTA |
| `styles.css` | Shared dark-mode-first design system with responsive breakpoints |
| `scripts.js` | Shared JS for accordions, code tabs, sidebar collapse, smooth scroll, active nav |

## Key Features Implemented

- **Dark mode default** — Deep navy/charcoal (`#0d1117`) with electric cyan/green accents
- **CLI Setup Section** — 3 accordions (Apps, Themes, Headless) with single-open behavior; each has npm/yarn/pnpm code tabs
- **Product Cards** — 3 visually distinct pillars (Apps, Storefronts, Agents) with icons and CTAs
- **Collapsible Sidebar** — Smooth collapse/expand on `apps-build.html` and `agents.html`, with state persisted in `localStorage`
- **Responsive Design** — Mobile menu, grid collapses to 1-column on small screens, sidebar auto-hides on mobile
- **Cross-page Navigation** — All 5 pages link to each other consistently via the top nav and footer
